title: Build RAG Over Your PDFs, Part 2

scenes.text: Your PDF now answers back. Last time, we loaded our PDF, chunked it, and stored it in a vector database. [1] Today, we ask it questions, and get answers with sources. [2] Part two of our RAG build.

Here's the flow. [1] The user asks a question. [2] Chroma finds the four chunks closest in meaning. [3] We paste them into the prompt, as numbered sources. [4] The model answers, using only those sources. [5] And it cites the source numbers, so you can check.

[1] Here's the code. [2] Open the same database, and our docs collection. [3] Read the question, and ask Chroma for the four closest chunks. [4] Join them into one context, each labelled with its chunk ID, like a numbered source. [5] Call the model. The system prompt says, answer only from the sources, cite them, and admit when unsure. The user message holds the sources, and the question. [6] Print the answer. [7] And it replies with citations!

data.heading: Ask your PDF
lines: "Cite source numbers. If unsure, say so.",
output: Only dental treatment needed after an
accident is covered [12]. Routine care is not [13].

scenes.text: That system prompt does three important jobs. [1] Grounding. Answer only from the sources, not from memory. [2] Citations. Show which chunk each fact came from. [3] Honesty. If the answer isn't in the sources, say so, instead of guessing.

You can build a lot with this. [1] Ask questions to your insurance policy, or loan agreement. [2] Revise for exams from your textbook PDFs. [3] Or give your company a helpdesk bot, over its HR policies.

Here's a common mistake. [1] People think once RAG works for one question, it's done. [2] Test it with a golden set, from episode 33. Try questions whose answers aren't in the PDF, and check that it says, I don't know.

data.myth: If it answers one question well, it's done.
data.fact: Test with a golden set, including questions the PDF can't answer.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Why do we tell the model to answer ONLY from the sources? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] To reduce made-up answers, and keep it grounded in your document!

Let's recap. [1] Chroma finds the closest chunks to the question. [2] We paste them into the prompt, as numbered sources. [3] The system prompt forces grounding, citations, and honesty. [4] And we test with a golden set. [5] Next, build an AI agent with tools. Follow AI Maastaaru!
